correctness.rationale: Every root fixes u; e(0)=0 and e^2=0 follow. The root-block children count is binomial times k-power, each layer-one block contributes the displayed binomial h-power weighted by the number of layer-two points, and all choices form a bijection. All admissible block maps occur. Support and unique-root results have direct independent combinatorial arguments. Direct raw-map checker matched every block-character fiber over 32 root-block configurations.

Classical full-transformation root constructions are credited as strong antecedents. Residual possibility of an unlocated colored-tree count is acknowledged.

value.rationale: The power-map fiber above a canonical constant element of a congruence-preserving finite transformation monoid is an intrinsic, natural enumeration problem. The entire induced block character and arbitrary heterogeneous block sizes are resolved uniformly, producing nontrivial weighted combinatorial interactions and a sharp root-uniqueness threshold. The value does not depend on an unproved wider conjecture or on experimental novelty alone.
